text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A United Nations compensations body will discuss today (Monday) a claim by Kuwait Oil Company for losses incurred due to the 1990-91 Iraqi occupation of Kuwait. Most of Kuwait's oil wells were set on fire or damaged during the occuaption.
- The Central Bank says would pay 5.31 percent for the second half of 1996 on bad debt bonds kept by banks and investment institutions.
- Commerce and industry minister discusses bilateral cooperation with U.S. commerce official.
- Kuwait Investment Authority says Kuwaiti employees at firms included in the state privatisation plan have priority to buy limited amounts of their companies' shares.
- Most shares at the Kuwait Stock Exchange maintained their Saturday price levels.
- Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah in Britain on a private visit.
- Traffic accidents in Kuwait claim 213 lives in the nine months to September.
ARAB TIMES - Team of the World Health Organisation in
Kuwait to investigate polio situation in the country.
- Iraq's oil minister says the United States is first to take Iraqi oil.
- Interior ministry warns against keeping illegal weapons.
